images.title: The HCF tiles the room
images.purpose: Show the 12 ft by 16 ft room tiled with 4 ft tiles, 3 rows by 4 columns, naming 4 as the HCF.
images.composition: One tiled rectangle in the centre, wider than tall, with a short two-line caption underneath and white space all round.
exact_structure: One rectangle 16 units wide and 12 units tall, divided into exactly 3 rows and 4 columns of equal squares, 12 squares in total.
The squares are filled teal (#0072B2) with thin white grout lines between them.
The top left square is filled reddish purple (#CC79A7) instead, with the label 4 ft along its top edge.
A grey (#6B7280) dimension line along the bottom edge labelled 16 ft, and one along the left edge labelled 12 ft.
Below the rectangle, caption line 1: HCF of 12 and 16 = 4.
rejection: any number of rows other than 3 or columns other than 4, or any total other than 12 squares
the 16 ft side drawn shorter than the 12 ft side
images.takeaway: The HCF is the greatest common factor, and 4 ft tiles cover the room with just 12 tiles.
images.description: A 16 ft by 12 ft room covered by 12 teal square tiles in 3 rows of 4, one tile marked 4 ft, with the HCF caption.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Count the tiles along each side first (3 and 4), then multiply; link the tile side to the name HCF.

image_decisions.why: The tiled room links the definition of HCF to the tile count.
